To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cholestyramin treatment of guinea pigs produces compositional and metabolic changes in the low density lipoproten fraction of the serum.

cholestyraminewas shown to increase LDL receptor activity in animal studies, but the compositional changes induced by cholestyraminetreatment in LDL were found to have a major effect on the metabolism of this altered lipoprotein, and that these effects were not predicted by previous animal studies.

cholestyraminewhich is known to alter LDL metabolism by increasing hepatic LDL-receptors and LDL fractional catabolic rates (FCR) also alters LDL composition such that the cholesterol:protein ratio is reduced, the LDL is more dense and smaller, and the LDL is depleted of cholesterylester and phospholipids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cholestyramin on low-density lipoproteins.
the metabolism and composition of low density lipoproprotein (LDL), and the effect of bile sequestrant therapy on LDL composition and metabolism in the guinea-pig model.
the role of the LDL receptor in the metabolism of LDL in the guinea-pig.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the compositional and metabolic effects of cholestyramin on LDL are complex, that the effects of the drug on the LDL receptor are not simple, that cholestyraminine does not simply increase the FCR of LDL, but that it does increase LDL degradation in the guinea pigs, and that the effects are not due to changes in LDL receptor activity.

the effects of cholesterol sequestration are more complex than originally thought, but they are also less dramatic than previously believed, since they can be reversed by the addition of glucose to the LDL.
the compositional alterations in LDL produced by cholestyramin are not the primary reason for the enhanced clearance of the lipoprotein.
